H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
35-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and mild hypertension presents with a 5-day history of dry cough, runny nose, myalgias, chills, and occasional headache; exam shows mild pharyngeal erythema without respiratory compromise—consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper-respiratory tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry “hacking” cough and “cold” symptoms.  
• Onset & course: Began ~5 days ago (start of last weekend); symptoms persist but not worsening.  
• Associated symptoms: Rhinorrhea, generalized muscle aches, intermittent headache, chills.  
• Denies: Sputum production, hemoptysis, shortness of breath, wheeze, chest tightness, palpable neck glands.  
• Self-care/relief: Paracetamol taken intermittently; no ibuprofen.  
• ROS (pertinent negatives): No fever reported; no sore throat beyond mild scratchiness; no nausea/vomiting; no chest pain.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – diagnosed ~5–6 years ago; home glucose monitoring “within normal.”  
   – Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Essential (mild) hypertension – well-controlled.  
   – Medications: Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• No other chronic illnesses documented.  
• Allergies: Not elicited (missing).

Social History:
• Location secure for confidential consult.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, occupation, and exercise habits: not discussed (missing).

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• General: Appears well on video.  
• HEENT: Mild pharyngeal erythema; no tonsillar hypertrophy/exudate.  
• Neck: No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy (patient-reported).  
• Respiratory: No audible wheeze; patient denies dyspnea. Chest not formally examined.  
• Vitals: None provided. Home BP this morning “within normal range.”  

Investigations:
• None performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold)  
  • Assessment: Classic URTI symptoms ≤1 week, benign throat findings, no lower-airway signs.  
  • Plan:  
    – Symptomatic relief: Advise OTC combination cold remedies (Day Nurse/Night Nurse) compatible with current meds.  
    – Continue paracetamol as needed; maintain hydration and rest.  
    – Red flags: Seek care if new shortness of breath, wheeze, chest pain, high fever, or if symptoms persist >3 weeks or worsen.  
    – No antibiotics or prescription medications indicated at present.

Issue 2 – Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stable  
  • Plan: Continue metformin; continue home glucose monitoring. Report any persistent hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, or illness-related glucose concerns.

Issue 3 – Hypertension, stable  
  • Plan: Continue lisinopril; continue home BP monitoring. No changes required today.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection – High likelihood: 5-day dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias; benign exam.  
2. Influenza / influenza-like illness – Moderate likelihood: Systemic aches/chills fit; absence of fever and mild course make this less probable.  
3. ACE-inhibitor–induced cough – Low to moderate likelihood: Dry nature fits but acute onset with viral prodrome argues against.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: Allergies, comprehensive medication doses, smoking/alcohol history, full vitals (temp, HR, RR, BP, SpO₂).  
• Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational fillers but medically intelligible.
